subject: POC: prompt set + eval dataset collection / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Williams <alex.williams@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: POC: prompt set + eval dataset collection / next steps

Hi Alex — great call today, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we can move to a kickoff next week: 

Recap
- Goal: Validate Redwood can meet Acme Health's throughput (200 reqs/min), latency (p95 < 350ms), and response quality for clinical summarization prompts described in the demo.
- Success criteria (proposed):
  * Quality: >= 85% pass rate on the evaluation rubric (fidelity + safety) across the provided prompt set
  * Latency: p95 < 350ms on Dedicated pool with 8x A100-equivalent GPUs
  * Stability: sustained throughput for 30 minutes at target load without errors

What we need from you to build the eval set
1) Prompt set: list of ~200 real prompts or representative queries you want evaluated (CSV or JSONL). Preferable columns: prompt_text, intent, expected_output_short (optional), sensitivity_flag
2) Sample logs: ~1k anonymized request/response pairs (JSONL) so our team can check formatting and build ranking/eval scripts
3) Success criteria confirmation: any modifications to the above proposed metrics, or business-specific pass/fail rules
4) Engineering contact for data/format questions (you mentioned Jacob)

Attachments: I’ve attached a short POC template that outlines ownership, timeline, and deliverables. (See attachment: redwood_poc_template.docx)

Proposed timeline
- Oct 6: kickoff (30-45m) with eng + security
- Oct 6-9: Redwood builds eval harness, ingests prompt set + sample logs
- Oct 10-16: Run evals, collect metrics
- Oct 19: Results review + next step decision

Owners
- Redwood: Marissa (program lead), Dev (integration/ingestion)
- Acme: Alex (product), Jacob (eng)

Immediate asks
- Please send the prompt set and the anonymized logs by EOD Oct 3 if possible. If you need a template, use the attached POC template or the CSV sample in the drive link.

Thanks — happy to be flexible on timeline if you need more time to sanitize logs.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC: prompt set + eval dataset collection / next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. Quick answers and attached files: 

- We can provide the prompt set and a sample of logs. Attached two files: prompts.csv (200 rows) and sample_logs.jsonl (~1,200 records). The logs are anonymized (patient identifiers removed), but include metadata columns we think are important (encounter_type, clinician_role).
- Success criteria: we agree with your quality/latency targets, but can we add a business rule that any hallucination rate measured > 5% on critical prompts (sensitivity_flag == true) is a blocker?
- Jacob will be our engineering lead on the POC (jmiller@acmehealth.com). He can answer questions about the log schema.

Proposed kickoff: Oct 6 at 11:00am PT works for our team.

Attached: prompts.csv (CSV, 58KB), sample_logs.jsonl (JSONL, 1.1MB)

On a related note, we have a standard data processing questionnaire — I can share it if you want, but for this initial run our security team asked only for a quick scoping call during the kickoff.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex
Alex Williams
Senior PM, Clinical AI
Acme Health

Thanks Alex — got the files. A few technical notes from our side: 

1) Schema: sample_logs.jsonl looks good. For ingestion we expect one JSON object per line with keys: request_id, prompt_text, response_text, timestamp, metadata. If you can include a small README (schema mapping) that will speed ingestion.

2) Sensitivity flags: please confirm which prompts are tagged as sensitivity_flag==true. We’ll treat those as critical for hallucination checks and run an augmented evaluator (QA + hallucination detector).

3) Data handling: for the POC we’ll ingest logs into a short-lived sandbox in our private cloud tenant; no persistent copy will be retained beyond 30 days unless you request archival. If Acme requires an S3/KMS integration or cross-account bucket access for us to pull logs, we can accommodate — Jacob please advise.

4) Output format: we’ll return per-prompt metrics (pass/fail, score, comments) plus a downloadable JSONL of model outputs for manual review.

I’ll start the ingestion script once we have the schema README and the sensitivity mapping.

Cheers,
Dev
Software Engineer, Inference Integrations
Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks for sending the files and for confirming the kickoff time. Quick confirmations and next steps: 

- Sensitivity blocker: we agree to treat hallucination rate >5% on sensitivity_flag prompts as a blocker. We’ll include that in the results slide and the pass/fail JSON.
- Jacob: would you please confirm whether we should pull logs via an S3 cross-account role or if you prefer to share a presigned URL? If S3 cross-account, please share the role ARN and bucket path; otherwise a secure presigned link is fine for this POC.
- Kickoff calendar invite: I’ll send the Oct 6 11:00am PT invite to all. Agenda: introductions, security scoping (15m), ingestion plan (10m), success criteria and milestones (10m), Q&A (5-10m).
- Deliverables: Redwood will deliver an eval report (metrics + examples), an artifacts bundle (outputs JSONL + scripts), and a short playbook for productionization recommendations.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
